"revision_justification": "This update clarifies the methodological boundaries and operational definitions of the existing preregistered study.

The revision makes the relationship between the fixed ten-object research corpus, six predefined scholarly-infrastructure layers, and seven operational platforms explicit. It clarifies that OpenAIRE and OpenAlex are separate operational platforms within the same discovery-graph layer.

It also further specifies the role of Research Software Identity Audit (RSIA) as supporting research-control, evidence, provenance, and reproducibility infrastructure, rather than as an additional research object, operational platform, infrastructure layer, or prospective observation unit.

These clarifications improve the consistency between the Data collection procedures and Context and additional information sections and the original research contract.

No changes are made to the five research questions, fixed RS01–RS10 corpus, six infrastructure layers, seven operational platforms, 60 object-layer analytical units per observation point, sampling strategy, observation schedule, measured variables, derived-variable definitions, primary descriptive analyses, inference criteria, missing-data handling, or non-causal interpretation.

No additional research objects, analytical units, interventions, inferential models, or causal claims are introduced.",

"344-40": "This study uses a prospective longitudinal observational design with repeated measurements on a fixed set of ten research software objects. Each object will be observed across multiple scholarly-infrastructure layers, including source repository, archival repository, identifier registration, author registry, preservation archive, and discovery graph.
Observations will be collected at predefined time points following relevant software-release events. For each object-layer pair, timestamped states will be recorded, including observed, not found at the queried endpoint, rate limited, unresolved, partially verified, or fully verified, together with relevant identifiers, source attributions, and metadata fields.
The same objects will be measured repeatedly across time and infrastructure layers. Historical observations from earlier release waves will be treated as a fixed baseline, while the preregistered observation window will provide new prospective evidence.
The primary analyses will describe cross-layer propagation order, measurable latency where timestamps permit, metadata consistency or divergence, recurrence of previously observed aggregation behavior, and the frequency and location of failure, partial, unresolved, or correction states. No interventions are administered and no causal effects are estimated.",

"344-51": "The object-level sample size is fixed at 10 research software objects. Each object will be observed across 6 predefined infrastructure layers, yielding 60 object-layer units at each scheduled observation point. Because the study uses repeated measurements, the total number of attempted observations will equal 10 objects × 6 layers × the number of preregistered observation time points. Missing, rate-limited, unresolved, or failed observations will remain part of the attempted observation set and will not be removed from the denominator.",

"344-55": "Data collection will begin with the first eligible new software-release event occurring after this registration. Only observations collected after registration will constitute the prospective dataset.\nObservation will end after the final preregistered follow-up time point has been attempted for all ten objects across all six infrastructure layers. Query failures, rate limits, missing records, or unresolved states will be recorded as outcomes and will not by themselves extend the observation window.\nNo additional software objects, infrastructure layers, or follow-up observations will be added in response to favorable, unfavorable, or ambiguous interim results. Any extension of the observation window or addition of exploratory checks after registration will be documented explicitly as an amendment or post hoc analysis.",

"344-47": " The study uses a fixed corpus of ten predefined research software objects (RS01–RS10) observed across six predefined scholarly-infrastructure layers.

The operational platform scope consists of seven predefined platforms:

GitHub

Zenodo

DataCite

ORCID

Software Heritage

OpenAIRE

OpenAlex

These platforms map to the six infrastructure layers as follows:

Source repository: GitHub.

Archival repository: Zenodo.

Identifier registration: DataCite.

Author registry: ORCID.

Preservation archive: Software Heritage.

Discovery graph: OpenAIRE and OpenAlex.

OpenAIRE and OpenAlex are separate operational platforms within the same predefined discovery-graph layer. Their separate platform observations do not create an additional infrastructure layer or increase the number of primary analytical units.

The primary analytical unit remains one research software object × one infrastructure layer × one scheduled observation time point. Accordingly, the study retains exactly 60 object-layer units per scheduled observation point (10 objects × 6 layers).

Data collection follows a prospective longitudinal observational design with repeated measurements at preregistered observation time points following eligible software-release events.

For each research software object and infrastructure-layer pair, publicly accessible platform records and API endpoints within the predefined operational platform scope will be queried and documented.

Each attempted observation will retain, where available, its software-object identity, infrastructure layer, release-event timestamp, retrieval timestamp, relevant identifiers, creator and source attribution, version and family relationships, archival origin, discovery and preservation states, platform response status, pagination completeness, and any observable correction or metadata transition.

Observation states will be recorded using the predefined categories:

Observed.

Not found at the queried endpoint.

Rate limited.

Unresolved.

Partially verified.

Fully verified.

Evidence references and source attribution will be retained to support independent inspection. Raw or retained source evidence, normalized records, derived observations, and analytical interpretations will remain distinguishable.

Missing, incomplete, rate-limited, and unresolved observations will remain in the research record rather than being silently discarded or interpreted as evidence of absence.

Historical observations from earlier release waves will serve as a fixed baseline. Only observations collected after registration within the specified prospective observation window will constitute the prospective dataset.

Data collection will begin with the first eligible new software-release event after registration and end after the final preregistered follow-up time point has been attempted for all ten objects across all six infrastructure layers.

Research Software Identity Audit (RSIA) provides the supporting research-control, evidence, provenance, and reproducibility infrastructure for these procedures.

Its machine-readable research-contract mapping, fixed-corpus manifest, observation schemas, state taxonomy, counting rules, and evidence/provenance conventions operationalize the boundaries defined in this preregistration.

The archived RSIA releases document the progressive development of this supporting infrastructure, including initial research-runtime establishment, evidence reconciliation, evidence-integrity verification, correction lineage, archival integrity, and repository lifecycle reconciliation.

Retained-evidence packages, source attribution, verification records, and append-oriented correction documentation support the traceability and independent inspection of collected evidence and its subsequent handling.

RSIA supports the execution, documentation, validation, and reproducibility of the observational process. Its repository, software releases, engineering inventories, internal validation records, and operational monitoring are supporting research-control materials, not additional research-software objects, operational platforms, or prospective observations.

RSIA does not expand the fixed ten-object corpus, six predefined infrastructure layers, seven operational platforms, or 60 object-layer units at each scheduled observation point.

No additional research objects, infrastructure layers, operational platforms, or analytical units are introduced through the supporting research infrastructure.",
